description: FIRST MIRROR GOLDEN (BACKLOG P2 mirror feature — new modeling capability, the reflective sibling of the pattern feature). A CHIRAL right-triangle profile (vertices (2,0),(5,0),(2,4) on the XY datum — the right angle at (2,0), a 3 mm leg along +X and a 4 mm leg along +Y, a 5 mm hypotenuse) is extruded 6 mm into a triangular prism (volume 36 mm^3, entirely at x>0), then MIRRORED about the YZ origin datum plane (x=0). A three-feature TREE (sketch -> extrude -> mirror) evaluated through the same evaluate-tree path as the pattern/extrude goldens. v1 DESIGN DECISION (option B): a mirror REFLECTS the current body about the plane and BOOLEAN-UNIONS the reflection into the single body chain (design 7.6) — the SAME 'replicate the current body + union' semantics as the ADD pattern. The source prism sits entirely at x in [2,5], so it CLEARS the x=0 plane and the reflection lands disjoint at x in [-5,-2]: the union is a legitimately DISJOINT TWO-lump body of volume 2V = 72 mm^3 (multi-body parts are supported, MB-0 — a mirror does NOT force one connected lump the way a pattern does). REFLECTION PROOF (position/orientation, not a translation): the union's centroid.x is EXACTLY 0 (the body is mirror-symmetric about x=0). A pure TRANSLATION of this chiral profile that reproduced the same disjoint bounding box (a -7 mm shift in x) would place the reflected right-angle vertex at x=-5 instead of x=-2, giving combined centroid.x = -0.5 mm, NOT 0 — so centroid.x == 0 to 1e-9 is the machine-checkable reflection-vs-translation discriminator. Locks: the mirror handler + Shape.mirror reflection + disjoint fuse + assemble_lumps multi-body finalize, GProp over the two-lump compound, and (via the parametrized round-trip gate) STEP round-trip of a multi-body mirrored part.
derivation: Expectations are HAND-DERIVED analytic values, not recorded harness output (geometry-gates skill: a golden recorded from buggy output enshrines the bug). The seed body is the chiral triangular prism: the right triangle with vertices (2,0),(5,0),(2,4) has area 0.5 * base(3) * height(4) = 6 mm^2; the sketch is underconstrained (position DOF remain) with zero initial residual, so planegcs provably returns the input positions bitwise (same solver posture as the pattern/extrude goldens). Extruded 6 mm along +Z the prism has volume 6 * 6 = 36 mm^3, spanning x in [2,5], y in [0,4], z in [0,6].

mirror: reflect about the YZ origin datum (the plane x=0). Shape.mirror maps every point (x,y,z) -> (-x,y,z), so the prism's three base vertices (2,0),(5,0),(2,4) reflect to (-2,0),(-5,0),(-2,4) at z in [0,6] — a congruent prism spanning x in [-5,-2]. The reflection is a true handedness-reversing isometry: the reflected right angle is at x=-2 (NEAREST the plane, mirroring the original's x=2), where no translation of the original (whose right angle is at the LEFT, x=2) can put it.

the source x-interval [2,5] and the reflected x-interval [-5,-2] are DISJOINT (a 4 mm gap across x in (-2,2)), so the boolean union is a TWO-lump body (a Compound), not one connected solid. volume = 36 + 36 = 72 mm^3 (2V — the two lumps share no material, so no overlap is subtracted).

surface_area = 2 * (single prism surface). Single prism: two triangular caps (2 * 6 = 12 mm^2) + three rectangular sides — the base leg 3 mm x 6 mm = 18, the vertical leg 4 mm x 6 mm = 24, the hypotenuse 5 mm x 6 mm = 30 — so 12 + 18 + 24 + 30 = 84 mm^2 per prism; two disjoint prisms = 168 mm^2.

centroid: by the mirror symmetry about x=0, centroid.x = 0 EXACTLY (the two lumps' x-centroids +3 and -3 cancel — the single triangle centroid x = (2+5+2)/3 = 3). centroid.y = the triangle centroid y = (0+0+4)/3 = 4/3 mm (unchanged by the x-reflection and the z-extrude). centroid.z = 6/2 = 3 mm (mid-height of the extrusion).
bounding_box = [-5,0,0]..[5,4,6]: x spans the reflected lump's -5 to the source lump's +5; y in [0,4] and z in [0,6] are unchanged by the x-only reflection.

topology: two DISJOINT triangular prisms. Each prism = 5 faces (2 triangular caps + 3 rectangular sides), 9 edges (3 per cap + 3 verticals), 1 shell. The union is disjoint so no seams merge: 2 * 5 = 10 faces, 2 * 9 = 18 edges, 2 shells (one closed shell per lump — the exact count that proves the reflection landed DISJOINT, not merged; an overlapping/merged result would collapse to 1 shell with fewer faces).

mesh (linear 0.1 mm / angular default): per prism, each triangular cap tessellates to 1 triangle (2 caps * 1 = 2) and each rectangular side to 2 triangles (3 sides * 2 = 6), so 8 triangles per prism -> 16 triangles for the two lumps. Faceted per-face normals mean no vertex sharing across faces: a triangular cap contributes 3 corners (2 * 3 = 6) and a rectangular side 4 corners (3 * 4 = 12), so 18 vertices per prism -> 36 vertices for the two lumps (same faceting convention as the pattern/box goldens).

GLB byte size is deliberately NOT pinned here: it is asserted deterministic (byte-identical) by the runner within one kernel version, but pinning the absolute size would break on every glTF-writer upgrade without geometric meaning.
tolerance_rationale: Measured first, then set (geometry-gates skill: never copy a bound blindly). The reflection about x=0 (Shape.mirror) is an exact negation of the x coordinate, the fuse of two DISJOINT planar-faced prisms introduces no boolean-seam geometry, and GProp integrates planar solids exactly. Measured deviations vs the analytic values (2026-07-23, build123d 0.11.1 / OCCT 7.9, planegcs 0.8.0): volume EXACTLY 0.0, surface_area EXACTLY 0.0, centroid.x EXACTLY 0.0 (the reflection-proof assertion — a translation would give -0.5), centroid.z EXACTLY 0.0, all six AABB bounds EXACTLY 0.0; the ONLY nonzero residual is centroid.y = 4/3 mm, whose IEEE-754 representation through the GProp integral deviates 6.66e-16 from the analytic 4/3 (a pure float-representation residual, not a geometry error). Documented ceiling 1e-9 gives ample headroom for libm/platform variation across CI hosts while staying 100x TIGHTER than the standing planar 1e-7 bound, matching the pattern/box goldens' posture. The solver contributes zero error by construction (zero-residual start, solved == input bitwise). Loosening this bound requires a reviewed kernel-level justification recorded here and in docs/GEOMETRY-QA.md.
